plan.notes: Source: University of Pittsburgh, Pittsburgh campus, 2023-2024 Undergraduate Catalog [Archived Catalog], page titled 'Program: Computer Science, BS' (https://catalog.upp.pitt.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=223&poid=69375). The plan below is a faithful transcription of the catalog's official 'Sample Plan of Study' (eight Fall/Spring terms); course credits match the catalog's per-term totals exactly. The catalog presents the sample as customizable and assumes: (1) introductory programming completed before admission to the School of Computing and Information, (2) placement readiness for ENGCMP 0200, and (3) mathematics readiness for MATH 0220. GER = General Education Requirement (student-choice slots; the SCI catalog defines 14 GER categories). Elective slots are student choice and may support SCI's secondary-field requirement. One course must satisfy the Diversity requirement. The catalog notes that CS Upper-Level 7 may be used for departmental honors, and lists the Year-4 Spring slot as 'CS Upper-Level 7 or Elective'. The capstone slot is shown as 3 credits in the sample plan; the catalog allows the capstone requirement to be satisfied via an internship, directed research, or a capstone-designated project course (2-3 credits). CREDIT CAVEAT: the catalog states the BS degree requires 120 credits, but the catalog's own published Sample Plan of Study sums to 122 credits (verified against the catalog's per-term totals: 16+15+16+15+15+15+15+15 = 122). total_credits is therefore set to 122 so the plan's credit sum matches the transcribed official sample exactly; no credits were added or removed. Prereqs are included only where confirmed by official Pitt catalog pages (CS 0445 requires CMPINF 0401; MATH 0280 requires MATH 0220; CS 1501 requires CS 0441); all other prereq arrays are left empty rather than inferred. The 2026-2027 Pittsburgh catalog program page for this major was not reachable at collection time, so the latest accessible official Pittsburgh-campus catalog version with a published term-by-term plan (2023-2024) is used and cited by its actual catalog year.
